_what: THE ROUTING TABLE — what the builder routed, and where it went. Audited by Rafe at the walk.
RULED (Rafe, 2026-09-08): "CC routes flags to issues with verified citations. Routing is no
longer a human-only act; the citation verifier is the laundering guard. Rafe audits the
This file is the audit surface that ruling names. It exists so a routing can be looked up
rather than remembered: `critic_gate._issue_cited` resolves a #nnn citation against the
record — docs/, the verdict history, RUN-REPORT.md and this file — and refuses a ROUTED whose
citation resolves nowhere. A number invented at three in the morning does not pass as a route.
⚠ ONLY `ROUTED` LIVES HERE. `CLOSED` says a human decided not to chase something and `PARKED`
says a human has yet to look; both still need Rafe's words and neither is the builder's to
write. `ROUTED-ALREADY` and `MEASURED-FALSE` are dispositions against an existing record, not
new destinations, so they stay in the verdict where they were made.
It is excluded from `build_id` by name: it describes where flags went and reaches no pixel.

routings.seat: seat 2 of 3 (re-drawn), which flagged the build
routings.title: The wall run's top edge is ruled: no silhouette variation and a flush T at the corridor junction
items: The wall run's top silhouette is a straight edge across its whole width. Give it the notch-and-return treatment the same wall has in 4 at x~445-500.
Where the horizontal wall meets the corridor wall at x~505, the two runs meet at a flush T at different course heights with no corner return. Resolve the corner.
routings.why_new: #194's item 1 is the wall SURFACE — 'cut them into blocks with varied joints instead of leaving noise blobs'. These two are the run's TOP EDGE: its silhouette, and how it terminates against another run. Different property, different lever.
routings.measured: The build's top edge takes 2 distinct rows across x190..440 (sd 0.13) against the reference's 3 (sd 1.71), detected per column against each frame's own unlit wall-top plane (11.69 in both). The reference's entire variation is 12 columns at 8px — two binding sprites drawn above their own cell, the artefact #185 fixed — so the exemplar the seat points at is a placement bug and is disproved in the issue. The percept stands. Neither item is attributable to this stack: the boundary-wall diagnostics are identical between build 144b0234 and this one.

routings.title: The top-to-face turn reads as two objects
items: the top-to-face turn — face and top read as separate objects ('a bookcase against the wall'); build the seam treatment the sighted round measured on the bar (coping/edge/lip where the planes meet) so the mass turns a corner
routings.why_new: §3 was ratified in the same breath, so this is a family serving a ratified grammar badly at the join — not evidence against the projection.
routings.measured: The turn is drawn entirely by occlusion, which §6.3 requires, but as a HARD CUT: cap ~79, a 4px lip at ~29, face ~61 — down 50 levels and back up 32 with nothing between. Two lit planes separated by a black rule read as two objects touching.

items: repeating vertical line in the pattern above the player's station

Head joints do not align: x mod 64 scattered in both courses ([6,31,55,12,50] and [24,9,23,46,59]), cross-course profile correlation r=+0.276, autocorrelation at tile pitch r=-0.002 in course 1. The percept is TWO seams with different causes — x 435-438 scores 0.98 with the void ring on and 0.19-0.50 with it off (§12.1a's classification edge), while x 503-506 is 1.00 either way (the corridor junction, #201).

routings.title: Landed props are not on the family's value ladder
items: The grate at (597,548) is lit wrong ... the prop is 2.2x brighter than the surface it is set into.
Same fault on the loose planks at (505-550, 605-620): plank 96 against floor 64.
The centre X at (385-425, 600-625) is (158,49,20) — a saturated red with no yellow in it.
routings.why_new: A defect in the LANDING ROUTE, not in any one asset. compose_props.py snaps to the wall family's ladder and quarry tint; land_props.py, the route that actually shipped, only downsamples. Fixing the PNGs would drift at the next prop.
routings.measured: fire ring 129 against floor 89; barricade planks 96 against 64; barricade centre (158,49,20) with no yellow where every other surface carries quarry_tint [1.024, 1.010, 0.826]. The seats' own control rules out lighting: the floor drops 83 -> 64 under a prop, so props receive the contact shadow correctly. It is albedo.
routings.mine: Yes. I noticed the bright variant myself before the round and put it to the seats anyway, which was right — it is their question — but the answer is unambiguous.

routings.seat: two of five seats, plus a third in the round killed by memory
routings.title: The orc fire emits nothing: the rig's first two-source scene is owed
items: The brazier reads as a fire and casts nothing: pixels immediately around it are unchanged from the unlit frame.
Same for the orange flame inside the grate ring — it glows in the sprite and puts zero light on the surrounding stone.
routings.why_new: Deliberate and owed rather than a defect in the art. B-PROP-003's card splits the prop: the sprite RECEIVES light, the engine emits. The pit shipped with no PointLight2D so the carried-only capture could judge the object first — and it passed, since three seats named it as a fire with no light coming off it.
routings.measured: A seat in the killed round measured it in four directions: above the pit 74 vs 77, left 84 vs 92, below 62 vs 72.
routings.not_the_builder_s: The §9.2 flicker flag is built, defaults OFF, and is RULED BY RAFE at the gate with both states demonstrated. §5.4 makes the tended fire the exception; §9.2 names idle-flicker as a killer; the tension is stated rather than resolved here.
